reason: Pulsatilla study links Julian flowering date to estimated bee visitation and seed set, but it does not identify a plant-minus-partner or overlap exposure with a focal partner activity curve. Retain as timing-mediated pollination evidence, not strict H1 synchrony.

Experimental flowering weeks, visitor composition/rates and single-visit seed set are measured, but the authors state comparable insect phenology data are unavailable. Calendar week cannot be prospectively ordered as partner synchrony without using pollinator effectiveness/seed outcome itself, so the week slope is retained as timing sensitivity rather than strict H1.

Early versus late Silene stellata windows switch from Hadena-dominant to co-pollinator-dominant regimes but are not a quantitative synchrony metric. Year-specific final-fitness contrasts remain in timing_sensitivity_effects.csv.
Peucedanum flowering date is positioned relative to a known seasonal seed-predator oviposition window, but partner activity is not measured as a matched continuous population-year overlap exposure.
Four-year Peucedanum selection mosaic is strong timing evidence but does not provide the same explicit synchrony exposure required for strict H1.
Predator presence changes selection on Gentiana flowering time, but a continuous partner-activity overlap exposure is not measured.

Silene vulgaris links seasonal flowering position to pollination, Hadena predation and final seed set, but no independently measured Hadena activity curve identifies a strict plant-partner synchrony exposure.

Ficus pumila directly measures receptive-fig phenology and Wiebesia emergence and documents seasonal abortion/seed failure, but no synchrony-to-final-seed effect with recoverable sampling variance is estimated.

Tripolium study shows early flowers escape attack and infers a lag before high ovipositing-female density, but the partner activity/emergence curve is not independently measured as the exposure. The inferred lag cannot satisfy strict synchrony H1.

Pinned public Maxfield 2021 raw data were reconstructed under the prospectively frozen leave-one-out overlap contract. The control-normal subset yielded n=11, r=-0.0522490931, Fisher z=-0.0522967173, variance=0.125. The registered direct-effect row is locked by CI to the pinned raw-data reconstruction.

Flowering onset was experimentally shifted and contemporaneous visitor rates/composition plus final seed set were measured, but no independent partner-activity curve or predeclared matching metric orders the four weeks by plant-partner synchrony. The null seed-set result remains valuable timing-sensitivity evidence.

Snow and greenhouse manipulations shifted Claytonia flowering and measured visitation, fruit/seed set and pollen limitation, but the study explicitly attributes early costs largely to frost and late costs to low visitation rather than identifying a direct plant-partner mismatch variable. Retain as multi-mechanism timing evidence.

Factorial flowering-week × water manipulation measures visitation and seed production, but calendar flowering week is not converted from an independently observed pollinator activity distribution into a registered synchrony/mismatch exposure. Retain as timing/abiotic sensitivity, not strict H1.
